claims.statement: The recast EU Energy Efficiency Directive requires local heating and cooling plans in municipalities above 45,000 people to map potential including waste-heat recovery.

The directive requires data centres above 1 MW to use waste heat or another recovery application unless technical or economic infeasibility is shown, and calls for installation-level cost-benefit analysis for defined new or substantially refurbished facilities.
Hypothesis: matched exclusivity can be sold or carried into a third-party-financed project; viable pairs, option terms and investor demand are unvalidated.

contrary_evidence: The directive expressly allows infeasibility findings and exemptions for imperative legal, ownership or financing reasons, so regulatory attention does not guarantee a project.
A source-sink map is not defensible unless backed by data access, route feasibility and enforceable bilateral option terms.

economics.acquisition_route: Desktop-screen one region, commission expert review of three pairs, and pursue only one dual letter of intent before spending on route or full feasibility work.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated path: three annual closes at PLN 900,000 average net development revenue create PLN 2.7m revenue and perhaps PLN 1m operating profit; a 4x operating-profit business value plus separately valued, non-overlapping retained carries above PLN 2m could put a 75% founder stake and accumulated cash over PLN 5m in 8-12 years. This is highly milestone-dependent and no option value is assumed before diligence.
economics.founder_time: 10-18 hours per week for mapping, commercial structure and partner coordination, with a one-live-project cap until external project management is funded.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Unvalidated estimate: 40-60% after thermodynamic, network, route, legal and financial specialists; failed matches and multi-year cycles materially lower portfolio returns.
economics.payback: Unvalidated target: 24-36 months from the first development close; retainers must cover early work because a complete project may never finance.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated hypothesis: PLN 20,000-60,000 feasibility retainer plus PLN 300,000-1.5m development fee or 2-6% carried project interest at a defined close milestone.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Each project is lumpy, but large source owners, ESCOs and district networks can repeat across sites; option quality drives referrals more than subscription retention.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: a proprietary heat-source/sink map, standardized option documents and a history of credible matches create early access to bilateral opportunities
fingerprint.customer: waste-heat owners and heat users, with district-heating operators, ESCOs and infrastructure investors as development buyers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: energy auditors, municipal heating plans, engineering firms and the regional renewable network identify sources and sinks; infrastructure partners fund construction
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: geospatial match, load and temperature screen, dual exclusivity, route diligence and investor-ready data room sold as development rights and success fees
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: source or sink pays a feasibility retainer and the project investor pays an origination fee or carried-development interest only at signed offtake, investment approval or financial close
fingerprint.problem_trigger: a new or refurbished high-energy facility faces heat-use assessment, a municipality maps heat supply, or a heat buyer seeks lower-carbon stable supply

founder_fit: Uses quantitative geospatial and energy modeling with strong AI leverage.
Connects to renewable and installation-sector relationships without requiring the founder to finance infrastructure.
A strict one-project pilot can coexist with employment.
Specialist engineers and investors can carry technical execution after an analytically strong origination wedge.
risks: Most apparent matches can fail on temperature, seasonal load, route distance or connection capex.
Exclusivity may be non-assignable or too short for infrastructure development.
Source shutdown, sink credit risk and competing heating plans can strand development work.
This is a relationship-intensive, long-cycle business that may not fit part-time execution without a partner.

structure.control_point: matched exclusive representation or option agreements covering a specific heat source, sink demand window and connection route diligence
structure.critical_dependency: temperature, load shape, distance, land route, permits and third-party project finance must support an economically feasible physical connection

thesis: Map Polish data centres, food plants, wastewater facilities and other steady heat sources against nearby district heating, greenhouse, pool and industrial heat demand. For the most credible pair, secure matched time-limited exclusivity to represent the waste-heat output and negotiate the sink's offtake, then package feasibility and route rights for an ESCO or infrastructure investor. The founder does not finance pipes or promise delivery; value comes from controlling a bankable bilateral option before the source and sink find each other.
title: Waste-Heat Offtake Option Studio
uncertainties: Which Polish regions have source-sink pairs within an economic distance and compatible load shape?
Will facilities disclose the operating data needed before exclusivity?
What option terms will an infrastructure investor recognize as bankable?
Can retainers cover expert diligence while keeping total founder capital below PLN 100,000?
